title: Driver lifecycle simplification + first console visual pass

driverControls: Remove manual Leaving / On the way / Arriving soon / Arrived rider-update choreography from primary driver controls
Primary rider ride flow becomes Accept -> Start pickup -> Pickup -> Start ride -> Drop off / Complete
Generate rider-facing status events automatically from deterministic driver actions and foreground GPS
Do not automatically launch an external map when a Pulse ride starts
Keep navigation available inside the Pulse driver experience
consoleVisual: Upgrade request and Scheduled cards to a cleaner ride-app hierarchy
Scheduled card: time, pickup -> destination, fare, single primary action
Request card: route, time, fare, Accept / Decline
Active ride: destination, fare, current phase and one dominant next action
Reduce technical labels and internal-state language
Preserve current live map and shift controls

acceptance: Driver does not manually tap Leaving, On the way, Arriving soon or Arrived as separate required steps
Starting a Pulse pickup does not force-open another maps/browser window
Fare is visible before accepting a rider request
Confirmed Scheduled rides show fare and one clear next action
Rider still receives a coherent status progression
Uber-mirroring workflow remains usable during development
